scores.name: Coverage
scores.rationale: All five bundled capabilities (dual-authorization, margin validation, 250ms SLA, circuit-breaker queuing, pacs.008 messaging) have functional, boundary, and negative cases (TC-001 through TC-022), including the previously missing negative/zero trade amount case (TC-022). Given the quality report rates the requirement 'bad' on negotiable/estimable/small due to bundling undefined thresholds, this is strong coverage of what is actually specified; it does not cover circuit-breaker recovery, confirmation-delivery failure, or dual-authorization timeout because the requirement never defines those behaviors, which the suite's assumptions explicitly acknowledge as a deliberate scoping choice rather than an oversight.

scores.name: Completeness
scores.rationale: Nearly every case has concrete, distinct preconditions, ordered steps referencing specific dollar amounts or currency pairs, and a verifiable expected result (e.g. TC-006/TC-007 specify exact boundary amounts of $1,000,000.00 and $1,000,000.01). A few validation cases (TC-014, TC-015, TC-016, TC-022) share near-identical preconditions and step phrasing, slightly reducing depth per case, but each still names the distinct invalid field or value being tested.

scores.name: Traceability
scores.rationale: Every one of the 22 cases carries requirement_reference REQ-108 and maps directly to a specific bullet in the requirement (threshold amount, margin validation, 250ms SLA, Tier-2 circuit breaker, pacs.008 messages). No orphan cases exist. The suite's assumptions list explicitly documents where it extrapolates beyond the literal text (e.g. exclusive $1,000,000 boundary, inclusive 250ms boundary, two-distinct-approver rule), keeping those extrapolations traceable rather than hidden.

scores.name: Correctness
scores.rationale: Expected results match the requirement's stated behaviors (blocking unauthorized large orders, rejecting on insufficient margin, queuing on Tier-2 volatility, emitting pacs.008 on completion). Where the requirement is silent (exclusive vs inclusive boundaries, dual-authorization mechanics), the suite states its interpretation as an explicit assumption rather than asserting it as fact, which is the correct handling of a requirement rated 'bad' for unambiguous, but those interpretations remain unverified against real business rules.

scores.name: Uniqueness
scores.rationale: Most cases are genuinely distinct scenarios (auth granted vs blocked vs single-approver vs same-approver-twice; margin pass vs fail vs exact-match; SLA at-boundary vs over-boundary). However TC-017/TC-018/TC-019 (USD/EUR, USD/JPY, GBP/USD) and TC-014/TC-015/TC-016/TC-022 (missing amount, malformed currency, missing counterparty, zero/negative amount) are template-repeated variations differing only in the substituted data value, which lowers the effective uniqueness of the suite even though each is individually justified in the assumptions.

overall.verdict: Strong, well-traced coverage of every capability the requirement actually specifies, with mature and explicit handling of its ambiguities and previously identified gaps; remaining work is to reduce templated redundancy and add an explicit positive-path check for counterparty risk verification.

gaps.detail: No case explicitly asserts that bilateral counterparty risk verification executes and passes for a recognized counterparty; every passing case (e.g. TC-001, TC-002) treats a passing check only as an assumed precondition, never as an observed step with its own expected result.

No case covers what happens to a queued order once market volatility drops back below the Tier-2 threshold (recovery from the circuit-breaker state); the suite's own assumptions acknowledge this as an open gap tied to the requirement's undefined recovery rule and deliberately did not invent behavior for it.

No case covers failure or retry behavior when pacs.008 confirmation message delivery itself fails after a successful settlement; the suite's own assumptions acknowledge this as an open gap tied to the requirement's silence on message delivery failure.

recommendations.detail: Add a functional test case where a recognized counterparty is submitted and the test explicitly observes/asserts that the bilateral counterparty risk verification step returns a pass result as its own checkpoint, rather than only assuming it via precondition text.

Consolidate TC-017, TC-018, and TC-019 (USD/EUR, USD/JPY, GBP/USD settlement) into a single data-driven test case with three parameterized currency-pair rows sharing one set of steps and expected result, unless per-pair regulatory traceability requires them to remain separate cases.

Consolidate TC-014, TC-015, TC-016, and TC-022 (missing amount, malformed currency code, missing counterparty identifier, zero/negative amount) into a single parameterized field-validation test case with one row per invalid input, since steps and expected-result phrasing are otherwise identical across all four.

Before adding circuit-breaker recovery, dual-authorization timeout, or confirmation-delivery-failure test cases, request that the requirement define: (1) the numeric Tier-2 volatility threshold and the rule for returning a queued order to normal processing, (2) the timeout/expiry window for a pending second approver, and (3) the retry/alert behavior when pacs.008 delivery fails. Do not invent these behaviors in test cases until specified.
